# Compatibility smoke matrix (early alpha)

This is a small, one-time benchmark, not a permanent test subsystem or a
claim about ecosystem-wide node compatibility. It answers one narrow
question: *can a representative set of normal Node-RED flow behaviors run
unchanged on top of this Temporal-backed execution runtime?* Every row
below reuses an existing automated spec or an existing manual demo as
evidence - no new automated specs and no new fixture files were added for
this benchmark (existing fixtures already covered every category below).

Base: Node-RED `5.0.7` (this fork's pinned upstream tag, per `AGENTS.md`),
Node.js `>=22.9`, `@temporalio/*` `1.24.0` (this package's `package.json`).

## Exact results (do not combine these into one invented percentage)

- **Node/runtime-mechanism cases** (capture layer, bootstrap, worker
  wiring, deploy lifecycle, credentials/context): **8/8 PASS**
- **Flow-pattern cases** (routing shapes a real flow author would build):
  **10/10 PASS**
- **Manual/external-gate cases** (not CI-run, human-executed): **2/2 PASS**
  (both re-run/re-verified as part of prior issues, not re-executed in
  this pass - see limitation notes below)
- **Combined full `@tbrandenburg` unit suite** (all specs, all
  categories, run fresh in this session):
  **156/156 passing** (`../../node_modules/.bin/mocha
  "test/unit/@tbrandenburg/node-red-temporal-runtime/**/*_spec.js"
  --timeout 20000`)

These counts describe **only the tested cases below**. They must not be
read as "X% of Node-RED node types" or "X% of the Node-RED ecosystem" -
the tested population is a deliberately small, representative set of
flow patterns and runtime mechanisms, not a survey of contrib nodes.

## Matrix

| # | Case | Node-RED / Node version | Evidence | Result | Limitation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Scheduled source ingress (Inject-style timer firing starts exactly one Workflow) | 5.0.7 | `worker_spec.js`: "M5/AC3: a scheduled Inject firing 3 times starts 3 distinct executeFlow Workflow Executions, no CLI start used" | PASS | none |
| 2 | Ordinary transform node (Change/function-style single hop) | 5.0.7 | `workflows_spec.js`: "walks a single path node-by-node until a send has no further wiring" | PASS | none |
| 3 | Multi-output node (each output port routes only to its own wired destination) | 5.0.7 | `workflows_spec.js`: "multi-output routing matches Node-RED: each output port's own send reaches only its own wired destination" (issue #13) | PASS | none |
| 4 | Two `node.send()` calls on the same port (not deduped) | 5.0.7 | `workflows_spec.js`: "does NOT dedupe two distinct sends on the SAME port - both destinationIds are enqueued"; `capture_spec.js` M2-2/M2-6 (issue #12) | PASS | none |
| 5 | Fan-out (one output wired to multiple destinations) | 5.0.7 | `workflows_spec.js`: "fans out to every destination wired on a port (branch: A -> B and A -> C)"; real-bootstrapped variant "executes all 5 nodes of a true fan-out flow" (issue #5) | PASS | none |
| 6 | Link In / Link Out | 5.0.7 | `workflows_spec.js`: "Link Out -> Link In works with NO bespoke Link routing (Link Out's own wires are empty; destinationId alone drives it)" | PASS | none |
| 7 | Catch node (handled node error routes to Catch, Workflow completes normally) | 5.0.7 | `workflows_spec.js` + `activities_spec.js` (issue #32): "a handled Catch route is enqueued and the Workflow completes normally instead of failing"; "a node error routed to a wired Catch node resolves with sends, no error, plus a handledError marker" | PASS | An unhandled node error (no Catch wired) still fails the whole Workflow by design - see `workflows_spec.js` "an unhandled node error ... still fails the Workflow". |
| 8 | Complete node | 5.0.7 | `workflows_spec.js`: "a Complete node's own real Node-RED routing is captured and reached by the Workflow (no error path involved)" | PASS | none |
| 9 | Join / fan-in (count-based) | 5.0.7 | `workflows_spec.js` (issues #24, #31): "real Join node (count-based fan-in) completes successfully - wave-based drain plus msg-identity ALS fallback fix both the scheduling deadlock and the capture.js correlation bug" | PASS | Previously a documented KNOWN LIMITATION (fixed by #24/#31); no remaining known Join limitation. |
| 10 | Nested subflow (instance-in-instance) | 5.0.7 | `workflows_spec.js` (issue #33): "nested subflows - internal hops at BOTH levels ... are routed locally by Node-RED and never suppressed/timed out; only the hop leaving the outer subflow's boundary is captured" | PASS | none |
| 11 | Finite loop (self-wired node, bounded) | 5.0.7 | `workflows_spec.js`: "a finite loop (self-wired node decrementing a counter) executes and terminates normally"; issue #34: "a finite loop below the configured maxNodeExecutions limit is unaffected" | PASS | An unbounded/misconfigured loop exceeding `maxNodeExecutions` fails fast by design (non-retryable `FLOW_EXECUTION_LIMIT`), not silently - see next row. |
| 12 | Execution-limit guard (runaway loop protection) | 5.0.7 | `workflows_spec.js` (issue #34): "a loop that would exceed maxNodeExecutions fails fast with a non-retryable FLOW_EXECUTION_LIMIT error instead of running to natural completion"; "every scheduled node invocation in a fan-out wave counts toward the limit, not just one per wave" | PASS | This is an intentional guard, not a bug: flows that legitimately need more hops must raise the configured limit. |
| 13 | Credentials / config node sharing | 5.0.7 | `credentials_context_spec.js`: "a credential-bearing config node's credential reaches a live node through Node-RED's own credential machinery"; "two nodes constructed from the same config node id share the identical live config-node instance"; "the credential value is persisted to a real credentials file, not left as an in-memory-only fake" | PASS | none |
| 14 | Node / flow / global context scoping | 5.0.7 | `credentials_context_spec.js`: "node context is private per node instance"; "flow context is shared across nodes within the same flow/tab"; "global context is shared across the whole runtime" | PASS | none |
| 15 | Persistent context survives a restart | 5.0.7 | `credentials_context_spec.js`: "a configured persistent (localfilesystem) Node-RED context store survives a bootstrap stop+restart with the same userDir" | PASS | Context/config state is worker-local; it is not itself made durable by Temporal - see "Known limitations" in `AGENTS.md`. |
| 16 | Headless redeploy / `flowVersion` change without process restart | 5.0.7 | `deploy_spec.js` (issue #15): "deploy() performs a real runtime.flows.setFlows() redeploy: new flowVersion, node instance recreated, new behavior live"; `worker_spec.js`: "new ingress after handle.deploy() carries the NEW flowVersion, without recreating the Worker/Activity" | PASS | An in-flight Workflow replay against a now-stale `flowVersion` fails loudly (`FLOW_VERSION_MISMATCH`), by design - see `workflows_spec.js` "throws a nonRetryable ApplicationFailure on FLOW_VERSION_MISMATCH". |
| 17 | Split Workflow-worker / Activity-worker deployment | 5.0.7 | `worker_spec.js` (issue #16): "createWorkflowWorker never calls bootstrap() and never boots Node-RED"; "createActivityWorker boots Node-RED, installs Capture, and registers executeNode on the Activity Task Queue"; "createCombinedWorker creates two independently-configured Workers when workflow/activity queues differ" | PASS | none |
| 18 | Worker-kill recovery (durable replay across a worker restart) | 5.0.7 | manual demo: `demo/flows.recovery-demo.json` + `demo/run-recovery-worker` (per-issue recovery gate) | PASS | Manual/human-run, not CI-automated in this pass; recovery is between-Activity only - an Activity killed mid-execution re-executes at-least-once on restart (side-effecting nodes like `http request` are not idempotent) - see "Known limitations" in `AGENTS.md`. |
| 19 | Representative binary/complex message crossing a Workflow/Activity boundary | `@temporalio/*` 1.24.0 | `serialization_boundary_spec.js` (issue #35); full shape table already published in this package's README "Message serialization boundary" section | PASS (with documented representation caveats) | `Buffer` round-trips as `Uint8Array` (not `Buffer`), `Date`/`Error` lose their instance type, and circular/function values fail loudly at the SDK's native conversion boundary - see README table for the complete shape-by-shape breakdown. |
| 20 | Real external source (MQTT broker, real wire protocol) | 5.0.7, external MQTT broker | `demo/mqtt-e2e-manual.md` + `demo/flows.mqtt-e2e.json` (issue #11): manual, human-run procedure confirming a real `mqtt in` node message starts exactly one Workflow Execution | PASS | Manual gate only, by design - MQTT's real wire protocol is intentionally outside CI (see `demo/mqtt-e2e-manual.md` for why). Not re-executed against a live broker in this specific benchmark pass; evidence is the existing documented procedure from issue #11. |

## Explicitly skipped (not silently omitted)

- **Contrib-node sanity check** (issue #36 step 3, marked optional/skip
  unless trivially easy): **skipped in this pass.** Installing and
  smoke-testing a real third-party contrib node (e.g. `node-red-contrib-*`)
  would add a new runtime dependency and/or a new manual step outside the
  hard anti-monster constraints of this issue ("no new permanent npm
  dependencies", "no CI matrix over contrib packages"). No contrib-node
  row is included above; this is an intentional scope cut, not an
  oversight.
- **No new combined manual smoke fixture was added.** The existing
  fixtures under `test/unit/@tbrandenburg/node-red-temporal-runtime/fixtures/`
  (`catch-flow.json`, `complete-flow.json`, `fanout-flow.json`,
  `join-flow.json`, `link-flow.json`, `loop-flow.json`,
  `multi-output-flow.json`, `multi-send-flow.json`,
  `nested-subflow-flow.json`, `credential-context-flow.json`,
  `scheduled-flow.json`, `subflow-flow.json`, `external-source-flow.json`,
  and the `demo/flows.*.json` manual demos) already exercise every row
  above without duplication, so a new one-off combined fixture was judged
  unnecessary.

## Explicitly unsupported

- **HTTP In / HTTP Response** — intentionally unsupported in the early alpha.
  These nodes depend on live Express `req`/`res` objects and are outside
  the durable serialization boundary. This does not apply to the outbound
  `http request` node, which is supported subject to Activity at-least-once
  semantics.

## Scope note

This matrix intentionally covers ~15-20 representative flow-pattern and
runtime-mechanism cases, reusing existing automated specs and existing
manual demos as evidence per issue #36's anti-monster constraints. It does
**not** attempt to test the broader Node-RED contrib ecosystem, and no
percentage or ratio above should be read as a claim about node types or
flows beyond what is explicitly listed.
